context: You're helping in the guesthouse kitchen and want to check your work before you get something wrong.

phrases.jp: こんな{感|かん}じですか。
phrases.note: Perfect when you show your work halfway through.

phrases.en: Is it OK to throw this away?

phrases.jp: これ、{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}そう？

dialogue_setting: In the kitchen, preparing dinner with your host.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: すみません、{野菜|やさい}の{切|き}り{方|かた}、こんな{感|かん}じですか。
dialogue.en: Excuse me, is this the right way to cut the vegetables?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.jp: うん、いいね。でも、もうちょっと{小|ちい}さく{切|き}ってくれる？
dialogue.en: Yes, good. But could you cut them a bit smaller?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.jp: この{皮|かわ}は{捨|す}ててもいいですか。
dialogue.en: Can I throw away these peels?

dialogue.speaker: Host
dialogue.jp: あ、それは{畑|はたけ}の{肥料|ひりょう}にするから、そっちのバケツに{入|い}れて。
dialogue.en: Oh, we use those as fertilizer for the field, so put them in that bucket.

kanji.where: On toilet doors, shower rooms and meeting rooms. When it's free, the sign shows {空|あ}き (vacant).
kanji.related: Related: {準備中|じゅんびちゅう} preparing (closed for now).

tip.title: Ask before you assume
tip.body: In Japan, doing something your own way without checking can cause more trouble than asking too much. ～てもいいですか (is it OK if…) is your best friend. If the answer is ちょっと…, it means no, said politely.

challenge.prompt: There's a bike outside the guesthouse. Ask the owner if you can use it to go to the supermarket.
challenge.hint: bike = {自転車|じてんしゃ}, may I use = {使|つか}ってもいいですか
challenge.model_answer: スーパーに{行|い}きたいんですが、{自転車|じてんしゃ}を{使|つか}ってもいいですか。
